source.title: TradeFM: A Generative Foundation Model for Trade-flow and Market Microstructure
source.authors: Maxime Kawawa-Beaudan; Srijan Sood; Kassiani Papasotiriou; Daniel Borrajo; Manuela Veloso

record.tranche_reason: Tests power-law scaling in a new setting: an autoregressive model trained on financial trade-event sequences rather than text.
record.gate_note: Appendix C reports fitted held-out-loss relationships for compute and dataset size. The paper uses Chinchilla scaling laws to guide model sizing, but does not test the compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Other results on market simulation and trading are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix C fits power laws to held-out next-token loss versus compute and dataset size for an autoregressive Transformer trained on financial trade-event tokens. This is a non-text setting, trained for 4 epochs on repeated data, so it bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present the scaling analysis as substantiating the foundation-model claim and say the plots show 'expected power-law relationships' between compute, dataset size and test loss. The paper's main conclusions concern market-simulation fidelity and zero-shot geographic transfer, not scaling.
record.recipe_differences: Uses held-out autoregressive loss and fitted power laws, but on proprietary financial event sequences and only three approximate model scales; it reports compute and dataset-size frontiers rather than a language-model parameter law or a compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.problems: The scaling analysis covers only approximately 125M, 250M, and 500M parameter models; the dataset is proprietary; no uncertainty for the fitted exponents is reported.

untested.parts: Image and video models, fine-tuning and transfer regimes. The scaling fit also does not separate repeated from unique data. Range is only about 0.6 orders of magnitude in parameters.
Not a language model; no parameter-count law is fitted.
No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Chinchilla 20 tokens/param is used only to choose model size; no compute-optimal fit is made.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Downstream fidelity (KS and Wasserstein distances) is reported only for the 500M model, not across scale.

missing.what: Out-of-sample perplexity versus epochs for all three model sizes. This bears on the repeated-data regime, but values are only plotted.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling result is a brief appendix claim based on three model sizes. Model size and token count were co-varied by design, so L(D) is not a clean data-only law. The paper does not say whether the frontier points are taken per epoch. V5 support is weak in breadth but is not contradicted.

versions.untested_parts: The model is for financial trade events, not language; the analysis does not isolate parameter count while holding other factors non-bottlenecked.
No reported test that fits on smaller runs and checks predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute search or reported compute-optimal parameter/token allocation trend.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests power-law relationships for financial trade-event modeling, with repeated data included; does not test image or video models, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes.
No downstream-task performance scaling or prediction from pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or setups to assess exponent sensitivity or disagreement between scaling laws.

rows.subject: TradeFM
rows.operation_detail: Fits a power law to held-out test loss on the minimum-loss frontier across compute levels.
rows.measure: Held-out test loss versus compute in Flops C
rows.note: The exponent and relationship are stated in the text; the underlying frontier is plotted.
rows.check: Link and state are right, but the evidence is thin. The fit spans only about 125M–500M parameters (under one order of magnitude). Training setups differ by size (batch 24/32/24, different GPUs and libraries). No goodness of fit or uncertainty is reported.

rows.subject: TradeFM
rows.operation_detail: Fits a power law to held-out test loss on the minimum-loss frontier across dataset sizes.
rows.measure: Held-out test loss versus dataset size in tokens D
rows.note: The exponent and relationship are stated in the text; the underlying frontier is plotted.
rows.check: Link and state are right. Dataset size is confounded with model size: each model was trained on its own Chinchilla-implied token count (2.6B, 6.4B, 10.7B). Four epochs of repeated data are included, and no uncertainty is given.

relationships.condition: TradeFM trade-event pretraining, 125M–500M models, 2.6B–10.7B tokens, 4 epochs, minimum-loss frontier
relationships.reason: Held-out loss fits power laws in compute (αC≈0.18, C1) and data (αD≈0.19, C2). The range is narrow and no fit quality or uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss fit compute and data power laws with exponents approximately 0.18 and 0.19, respectively, over a narrow range without reported fit quality or uncertainty.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TradeFM financial trade-event pretraining, for the reported compute and dataset-size frontiers
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports fitted power-law relationships for held-out loss versus compute and dataset size (C1, C2); this supports the claim in this tested non-text setting, without establishing it for other modalities or regimes.
